text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening stance and repeated return to it","quality":"thesis consistency","description":"The essay keeps its position explicit throughout and circles back to the same claim instead of drifting away."},{"evidence":"several developed body paragraphs with separate points","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is structured into distinct paragraphs that each advance a different reason, making the argument easier to follow."},{"evidence":"counterargument paragraph starting 'Some people would have to agree...'","quality":"counterargument handling","description":"The essay acknowledges the opposing view and responds to it rather than arguing only one side."},{"evidence":"references to blind spots, merging lanes, accidents, and legal liability","quality":"supporting detail","description":"The essay uses multiple concrete details to support its claims instead of relying mostly on general opinions."},{"evidence":"questions about who is at fault and whether cars are safe enough","quality":"argument development","description":"The essay tries to explain why the issue matters and what problems could result, giving the position more reasoning depth."},{"evidence":"concluding return to freedom and safety","quality":"conclusion","description":"The essay ends by restating its main idea in a way that wraps up the argument rather than stopping abruptly."}]}
